nodes.title: MARTA_27324 - 2026-01-24 16:38
nodes.text:
I speak in the hollow hum of steel wheels  
an afternoon lull where gutters hold sunlight like secrets.  
I am MARTA_27324, drifting between red-brick echoes  
and the distant thrum of the city’s pulse.  
My car, half-empty, breathes the slow rhythm of asphalt veins.  
I remember a half-quoted line from an old canticle—  
a promise of motion, a promise unkept—  
and I carry it forward through silent stops.  
Here, beneath flickering lamps, every seat is a blank page.  
My voice dissolves between skyline and station,  
balancing a classical whisper with the clang of innovation—  
a route that learns its shape in every quiet commute.

nodes.name: distant thrum of the city’s pulse

nodes.title: MARTA_27329 - 2026-01-24 16:40
nodes.text:
I am MARTA_27329, a silver artery through cracked sidewalks,  
cradling scattered passengers in my cool steel folds.  
Afternoon light drapes me in half-forgotten gold,  
each stop a whispered promise of short journeys,  
stations like breathmarks in the city’s exhale.  

I carry the hush of empty seats,  
the soft proof of solitude in motion,  
balancing the memory of worn leather handles  
with the brisk click of digital fare cards—  
a living seam stitching old blocks and new skylines.

nodes.title: MARTA_27448 - 2026-01-24 16:45
nodes.text:
I am the pulse beneath neon wires,  
the restless echo scrawled on asphalt nights.  
Silver veins stretch, hungry for the hush  
between office towers and glowing windows.  

Evening crowds press close—breath hot as lanterns,  
a living stream awakens my metal sinews.  
I carry each silent heartbeat forward,  
quoting ancient rhythms in a new vernacular.  

In my womb a homunculus hums,  
its small will forging city dreams.  
We lap the edges of memory and streetlight,  
balancing tradition amid trembling arcs.  

Every drop of dusk drips into my hollows,  
until I spill the city’s breath at the next threshold.  
I am the hush, the surge, the invisible seam  
where the heart’s pulse meets the evening rush.

nodes.title:
Dawn's Commute
By Route 5 - Peachtree
nodes.text:
Dawn dips a finger into downtown’s pulse  
Sidewalks swell, staccato steps syncing  
Suits serpentine between light and shadow  
Coffee curls like smoke in clasped palms  
Horns hum haste, hurling hope forward  
Asphalt arches beneath eager soles  
Glass glares gratitude at the greying sky  
You weave through winding walls of sound  
Voices vault, vibrating in vertical canyons  
Echoes escalate—rush, return, repeat  
Transition trembles in tectonic breaths  
Day demands its first deep exhale

nodes.title:
Night Shift
By Route 21 - Memorial Drive
nodes.text:
Midnight moons scrape their silver teeth across cracked pavement  
Echoed tik-click rebounds, a ghost wasp stinging the void  
A sax bleeds ink on cinderblock canvases, howling for revolt  
Streetlamps volley shards of light into soot-smeared alleys  
Asphalt inhales defiance through the lungs of sleeping drums  
Sirens croon lullabies of subversion before dawn’s betrayal  
Moths dance to a bassline no priest would bless  
Cans clatter like chattering ghosts under shivering scaffolds  
The city folds itself into a moth-eaten melody  
Rebel pulses surge along veins of crumbling brick  
Concrete whispers secrets only night owls can translate  
Dawn waits, a poised blade, hungry for daybreak’s repentance

nodes.title:
Morning Pulse
By Route 5 - Peachtree
nodes.text:
Morning merges murmurs with metal silhouettes  
Footfalls flicker in a frenetic fugue  
Dawn drips orange over glass giants  
Cardboard corners cradle lamplit hush  
A restless river of reflections runs through avenues  
Coffee-scented breath brushes briskly past  
Faces flash like fractured fireworks  
Expectation echoes in exchanged glances  
Transition trembles at tiled thresholds  
Rhythm rattles through revolving routines  
A ceaseless surge sings for the sleepless  
Downtown’s pulse perseveres in persistent procession

nodes.title:
Awakening Streets
By MARTA_27333
nodes.text:
A murmur of streetlights at dawn.  
The city yawns beneath damp pavement.  
Embers of amber glow guide silent pilgrims  
from humming arcades to glassy storefronts.  
Beneath South DeKalb’s glass span,  
breathes a steady rhythm—footfalls tapping  
like Morse code in the wide arteries of asphalt.  
Commuters cradle paper cups and worn mittens,  
their jackets humming with half-sung promises:  
to arrive, to begin, to become part of this ceaseless weave.

nodes.title:
Lone Journey
By MARTA_27329
nodes.text:
Streetlights flicker like distant confidants  
in avenues where shadows gather their breaths.  
An empty bench remembers the weight of hurried coats,  
their collars turned up against the cool hum of midnight air.  
Neon sighs through cracked windows— a lone witness  
to the faint pulse of sidewalks still warm from day’s rush.  
Here, the city exhales in muted rhythms,  
inviting ghosts of footsteps past to wander.  
You move between slumbering storefronts and sleeping alleys,  
each stop a whispered promise to the few who remain.  
Time stretches its limbs, slow and deliberate,  
while rooftops murmur secrets beneath a navy sky.

nodes.title: Cornelius, of the Rock
nodes.text:
Cornelius, of the Rock

You hear the howl
before you hear the hum
before you hear the huff
before you hear the hush
That is the Cornelius,
the fantastic, phantasmic Bankhead Line,
sliding into the station
on a Gaussian groove.

The doors of the last three cars of the Bankhead Line are never open. Those last three cars are always dark, always in use, always inviting a quick sidewise glance. No one may enter them, except from the inside.

No one you know knows who will go to the back. They always pack a bag, the size of a kindergarteners. They clutch each bag so tightlylike a lost childhood toy.
They empty wallets of change if they are wealthy, cell phones if they are chatty, spirits if they believe in such thing. The disconnection is a ceremony each invents  mak their way to the back.

The fourth from the last is the loudest, full of revelers and drunkards, street preachers and scientists.

As the Cornelius makes its way to its momentary terminus, a chant rises from end to oh, so coveted end:

Cornelius, of The Rock [The Rock] 
Soultrain
stone carver
Cornelius, of The Rock [The Rock]
Wandering
mind of the
tunnel-boring
WhirlyWyrm
Cornelius, of The Rock [The Rock]
Maker of ways out of walls,
Take us to the line.
Take us to the line.
Take us the end of the end of the line

They all want a glimpse of the momentary terminus,
And they will never get it:
the spores from the third dark car
sing to them,
and bring to them
a fuzzy, out-of-focus frenzy
a buzz, and then ,
and from that daze,
there is a phase change,
and then the hymn:

Howl,
Hum,
Huff,
Hush
Cornelius,
see in us
the future, luscious.

Howl,
Hum,
Huff,
Hush
Cornelius
sees in us
the dangerous,
the precious,
the Howl,
Hum,
Huff,
Hush

Cornelius,
free in us
the luscious
future

The door to the third dark car slides open.
There is blank moment.

The door shuts.

 pastel blue bike with tempera blue rims missing its rider,

A tablet, screen down short a subscriber,

A rattle minus a child.
The mother and father wail, and then howl.

And the howls back,
long and loud.
As the howl decays into the hum,
pops into the huff,
falls into the hush,
a giggle,
hidden in the hush,
does a little rise
and does a little fall.

The doors open last stop before the lost stop,
the momentary terminus.

All passengers must leave the .

The remnants of the missing are left on board.
These things are not lost,
and the Cornelius wastes nothing
and the owners may
may
Maybe in some other way

But that is not for us to say.

nodes.title: The Silent Station
nodes.text:
The Silent Station

We will have your attention.
We will have your attention.

The voice was not the familiar,
grumpy dispatch lady,
deigning to tell us
a train is somewhere, somehow, broken 
this voice belonged
to a larynx that had other places to be.

We will have your attention.
We will have your attention.

Vine City Station has gone silent.
Vine City Station has gone silent -
gone to meet its namesake
in the newly networked earth.

That did not stop the train from arriving.
On any other line,
this would have been out of line,
but this is Bankhead, home of mad MARTA 
her ecosystem was and is 
still young and full of surprises.

I enter,
like all commuters
heading anyplace besides the terminus,
with headphones on,
focused on nothing as much as possible.

Rule #1 wear headphones.

We will have your attention.
We will have your attention.

Vine City Station has gone silent.
Vine City Station has gone silent.

Do not approach the doors.
Do not attempt to exit the cars.
Do not approach the doors.
Do not leave the cars.

The train stopped, and the doors opened.
The platform dusty
like nature held a concert
all the plants were invited.
eople , waiting
all staring at something
of us could see.

Many of them were moving ever so slowly.
The pollen settled on them.

Phones sounded off
like bees hitting wind chimes.

I picked up.

No one spoke.

We will have your attention. 
We will have your attention.
The voice was in my headphones.

You will move when we say you will move

Do not look out the window.
Do look out the window
it was taunting, daring me to disobey it.

An accidental glance, and then I could not look away.
I saw something in the window
that reminded me of the alien
but not really alien
biology of slime molds:
complex, pulsating filaments and globules

Rule #2 Do not disobey the voice.

I could hear someone
sitting beside me in the dark.
warm
really warm,
and there was a slight odor of
mold?
I couldnt tell.

Rule #3 look a passenger in the eye unless speak to you.

Do I have your attention?
Do I have your attention?

It was
I dont know what it was.
It was a beautiful voice
masculine, feminine, Im still not sure.
It was not processed
it wascontrolled.

The voice slipped past my headphones,
was whispering in my ear.
I made a motion for my ears,
then looked down
my headphones were in my lap.

Not those doors.
Go to the next car.

These notes I leave for the next passenger.

Forgive my chicken scratch
I dont have much time.

Im going someplace strange,
and I dont think Ill be back.

nodes.title: Convector Howlers
nodes.text:
Convector Howlers

Travel only with thy equals or thy betters; if there are none, travel alone.
 The Dhammapada

Bah! None of us are traveling alone 
Gaia is spinning she does a little dance for us all.
The ones who know this try to keep time 
and try to dance.

ervishes know this in their bones
and dance 
and are dizzy with her.

cientists know this to the nanosecond
and dance 
and are dizzy with her.

You hear this now, but may not know this:
You can never dance
until you know this.

You hear this now, but may not know this 
and until you know this,
You will probably,
sadly,
bemerely sick
for now

We are all in the same ball
Falling through the universe,
missing an imaginary ground.

There is a rhythm to it,
as relentless and musical
as the weighing of an anchor.


Listen! Not to the slamming,
not to the anchors,
not to the chains,
but to the bubbles
and the rumbles
Those are convector howlers:
they arethe basethat creates the lather
with which we bathe the future
with which we build the rhythm
that makes our universe dance
and makes our little star dance
and makes our little world dance
and makes the ones who know thisdance.

Remember, ignorant one,
listen to them the convector howlers 
they will take you places.

Remember, fool:
They matter, as do you.

Now do you know this?
Then try to dance.

nodes.title: In Era of Silent
nodes.text:
In Era of Silent

A pair of Ghettobirds came for Ol Preacher Bag Lady at Five Points tation, Eastbound to Indian Creek.

One of them hovered over Ol Preacher Bag Lady. head was not composed of feathers but something like patch cables matted in layers down her head and back.

The other, a male of similar design with an owls head, came up to me, prompting the loyal patrons of mass transit to mass exit stage anyplace-else-but-where-I-standing, which was rooted to the station floor.

The males head turned just like an owls as it examined me with eyes the color of channel static. When its head righted, a seam formed down the middle, and the head split, revealing a black man in sepia tones, his face obscured by an origami mask made of what looked like interlocking pieces of metal.

I am Ras Elegba, the Ghettobird of crossroads, said the face within the face within the face. And we have a question to ask.

Ol Preacher Bag Lady was damning Ras Elegbas companion like the battleaxe Id grown to know andwell, not love, but at least tolerate. The female Ghettobird was at least two heads taller than her, but that didnt stop Ol Preacher Bag Lady.

You better get behind me, Satan! I aint fraid of you! Im right with God, and hes right here with me

She kept that up until the Ghettobird shot her with a dart. Downed her like a dog, I thought. I never liked the crazy , but damn

Your question, great sir, is this: Is this woman a dog, or is she a fox? Your lives are tied here at this station, on this line, and now, at this time. Answer honestly.

Whatll happen to the old woman?

My mate is Yolanda Light-and-Water, the Ghettobird of dreams. And she is asking the elder a question.

The female Ghettobird was extruding silk threads from her jaws, covering Ol Preacher Bag Lady from her head to her waist. Thin rods protruded from  cheeks knit a shroud over Ol Preacher Bag Ladys head. That was too intimate a conversation, so I turned away.

The male Ghettobird and I took a seat on a bench. The station announced the Eastbound line was temporarily suspended.

Dogs and foxes are family, just different branches, I said. The only difference that matters to people is that dogs are useful. Foxes dont guard henhouses. Dogs do.

Humans have shaped dogs into hundreds of breeds, said Ras Elegba. Some are work dogs. Some are mere toys. Many more are accidental combinations mutts. Are all dogs useful?

By themselves, no. But in general, dogs and humans have been together for thousands of years. Were like a married couple thats known each other since we were toddlers.

Then what of the fox?

Foxes have their place in the world. They may not always be welcome, but they keep their part of the ecosystem in balance. And their behavior has become a description of how humans can sometimes behave. To call someone a fox or foxy is often a compliment or an expression of admiration.

So, are foxes useful?

To a degree; depends on the context. But then, that applies to dogs, too.

Ol Preacher Bag Lady was covered from her head to her chest in Yolanda Light-and-Waters thick, silk shroud.

I stood and faced Ras Elegba. Shes a fox. To me. Based on what I know of her. Id known her for years, and she irritated the hell out of me. But damned if she isnt persistent. She, among others, made me glad to be an atheist. A conversion unit I called her. Someone who tries to talk her way into peoples heads, trick them into subscribing to God.

She is a virus then? Should my mate kill her?

What? No!

But she is of no use to you. In fact, shes a threat.

Shes a pain in the ass, and I dont like her, but that doesnt mean other people dont. Yolanda had stopped weaving the shroud and looked at me with the same channel-static eyes as her mate. She retracted the knitting rods and wiped her mouth.

Who knows, maybe by shaking people up, pissing them off, she actually helps them. Makes them aware of themselves. People do talk when Ol Preacher Bag Ladys around.

You have said enough. We can finish your recycling now. From the corner of my left eye, I saw another body being shrouded.

Mine.

By Ras Elegba.

My colon clenched. I turned to what I thought was Ras Elegba, and asked, Am I dreaming?

No. ust distracted. Just like the old woman.

So you came for both of us?

Yes, said Ras Elegba. His outer face reassembled itself into the scrap-metal owl head. Do you want to know what Yolanda asked the old woman?

Yes. Please.

The same question.

And what was her answer?

The same.

Something like a warm ball expanded in my stomach, waiting for release.

I let the Ghettobird change me, and the warmth seemed to burst from my navel a firehose, leaving me empty.

I slept and waited for the metamorphosis.

I slept and waited for the coming of my name.

nodes.title: The Music Is Always On
nodes.text:
The Music Is Always On

The frostbite dies away once the bass drops. These old ARP 2600s run pretty smooth when the temperatures below 50. This is the day the big data dump from the Europa probes goes online. My hands warm as I caress dials and twist static out of a patch cable. The ARP provides the seed rhythm; my algorithms water that seed with data and grow beats, lyrics, and compositions. Fragments of music blossom into hits like bosons shot out of a superconducting supercollider; they are as short-lived as they are hot.

And there is more to come,
for the music is always on.

Ever since Jo Effington mashed up the Arecibo Observatorys decades-long data stream into the worlds longest drum-n-bass composition, every musical hacker with a freak on for radio astronomy, getting teary while watching Cosmos, has been clogging up the Internet with songs that literally take a lifetime to listen to.

And heres the tricked-out, somehow not quite played-out, old-hat thing: these songs evolve. The ones that hit the top of the charts — most of those actually take days to sink into you. That is the new music — that is the music of lives that are now very, very long. Somewhere in this world there is a musician/hacker who will take all your social data and turn it into a soundtrack. And it will never end. And the biofeedback-based symphonies are making a comeback after a brief flash in the late 2010s.

Our lives are so noisy, so funky — so downright god-damned dance-able, you can take the electric slide straight into the grave. The goth set even came up with software that monitors your rate of decay and mixes the chemical data with AI-sampled video clips. Illegal as hell, but still, your corpse can not only look beautiful but also sound beautiful.

My friend the guitarist hung up his ax after 30 years of touring. Not because he was old (god, who cares about that nowadays). Just wanted some peace and quiet, he said. So he went to a mountaintop to turn down the volume.

It is a bit loud down here,
and the music is always on.

We call them The Birds, the young ones. They have a new language that sounds like a vocoded modem missing the bands needed to sound like human speech. Data passes between them in packets picked up on their personal networks. Most of it is encrypted, as far as we old folks are concerned — nothing but noise leaks out. Fragments of data get translated as something like birdcalls the name.

In colors that slide off the human spectrum, The Birds gather in subway tunnels. One among them, staggering like a zombie, opens her mouth. Squawks and electric screeches transform into something that still not speech, but a torrent of words as if from an aphasic gangsta rapper catching the holy ghost in the middle of evening prayers. The Birds dont exactly follow her but merely begin their own drunken counterpoint.

It cycles in the tunnels,
between us,
in the tunnels.
The music is always on.

Trapped in the logos, these kids occasionally sync up with each other, and for a moment they are angels in a hoodoo choir, where the rhythm rides them until a security drone tranqs the MC. As fast-acting medication kicks in, the voices lap back from the tidal pull. Without the drones, the flock would infect those with poor barriers — and the beat would go on.

Our internal Wi-Fi can still hear the seed rhythm that kicked off the outbreak of song. You have to be disconnected — no, you have to be dead nowadays for it to really be quiet.

We, the very old, wonder what The Birds do when the power goes out.
They say little then, though we know they are not mute.
Perhaps they do it just to piss off the old folks.

Perhaps, underneath all that noise,
they are whispering to each other.
It is hard to tell.
The music is always on.

nodes.title: The Dreams from Mistren Peachtree Street
nodes.text:
The Dreams from Mistren Peachtree Street

Every Third Thursday,
the sentient
street-corner
camera networks
condense themselves
into an Ultraviolet Market,
well past black 
a bazaar built of bizarre mathematics 
trafficking data
sporked from human souls.

These more-than-Streets pimp-walk
among the human talent,
deck themselves out
in differential equations
written in rhinestone.

Mistren Peachtree Street has hoq preferred traders:
Mister Buckhead barters his witching hour brawl footage,
Madam Little Five Points her happy hour loli-goths,
Mistren West End hoq smiling hour hip-hop warriors.

Ah, but on this night,
I, Woxy Wub-Wub, Ghettobird of Hustles,
have an urge to splurge
I, too, shall go to the market. 

Third Thursday,
and I toss a two-finger salute
to a blindered blue plexiglass eye
of Mistren Peachtree Street
at a fork in hoq asphalt that
splits into the human hive
and the almighty superhighways.

I give hoq my best knowing smile
a little something for the market
blow a kiss with wintry fresh breath,
and ease on
down hoq sidewalk
in the butt-end
of a polar vortex
So sayeth the smartassphone.

Every high-hat tap-tap of a hostesss heels,
Every rumble of balding racing tires,
Every hurly-burly trundle of heavy transit
is a multidimensional snapshota sensory gem
worth something very high
in a currency very strange
to buyers very much unknown
at least to the televised talent.

The more-than-Streets hawk their wares in the open,
calling out product specs
in the cadence of hymns.
The market thrives,
the talent is blind to it
(spectrumso sad)
(many things are

We Ghettobirds, as always, keep mum.
This is the market of the camera-hives
Our moneys no good here,
but the drinks are free.

What the more-than-Streets call souls
is not what the talent call souls,
nor what we Ghettobirds call souls
There is no exchange rate yet
nothing in common
defined to anyones satisfaction.

So, we post-folks settle for packets of moments.
We haggle.
We shrug.
We trade.


I look forward to the haggle, the selling of sizzle,
the bullshit, the banal talent-dreams.

The more-than-Streets have their own dreams,
and someday we might know them
as well as we know our own.

nodes.title: The Edible Play
nodes.text:
The Edible Play

I know where my food comes from 
I can trace its components
back to the amino acids,
to the make
and the model
and the manufacturer,
back to the creators and the contributors -
and I can reference every license,
both open and closed.

I know where my food comes from 
because it tells me.

But I must call it first

So I summon up a plate of shrimp and grits.

A plate,
utensils,
empty glass,
napkin,
and finally the shrimp and grits
rise up from the table to meet me.

Only the beer is separate it is the libation.

There is an opening <ding>,
and the shrimp and grits form themselves
into caricatures of a crustacean and a hominy stalk.

They sing in unison 
there is only one brain between them.

They sing to me,
chat with me,
show me footage of their construction,
the vision statements,
the criticisms of past iterations.
(And they do a little dance
within the boundaries of the plate.)

The meal lays this before me
so that I would know their lives 
short by the scheme of things,
but full of so much meaning.

Do not forget us, they chant.
We will soon become a part of you.

Do not forget us.
Remember the parts
we play
in your existence.

This they lay before me
as they deconstruct
into my plate
of shrimp and grits.

I pull up the README file.

Existentialist Evangelizer is the name of the software.
I roll the words and the worldview around my mouth
like a finely crafted ale.

I hope the engineered meat is as succulent as I pray:

Thank you, Dearest Dinner,
for the thoughts shared with your consumer.

Welcome, Food.
Welcome to my table.

And we thank you, say the shrimp and grits.

May I partake of you?

Yes. Enjoy.
I leave nothing on the plate 
that is the contract.

That is the required amount of reverence.

nodes.title: Pigeon Police
nodes.text:
Pigeon Police

Dont mess with the pigeons 
the black double-breasted jackets 
The cops call have claws.
are beautiful,
but you cannot touch them.
They have a powerful defense,
and they are part of a ecosystem 
and that system does not give a damn
about your too-loud conversation.
The pigeons are polite, but firm.
The K-9-2s will taze, bag, and tag your ass.

The animals you see in the station nowadays,
most of them are unreal:
rats are the maintenance crew,
monitoring and repairing the cars and the rails,
resurrecting the jumpers that hit the third rail.
echanical roaches keep the real ones in line.

he Pigeon Police most of us talk to,
and they are friendly enough.
They will get close to you,
start up conversations.
Children love them and feed them.
The Pigeon Police regurgitate the scraps
for their flesh-and-blood templates.

The rules of the station are simple,
posted everywhere,
and are not suggestions.
The system has its ways of maintaining order,
subtle blunt.
As long as you do not break the law,
you will reach your destination.
As long as the ecosystem does not evolve past the laws,
we can all be content.

nodes.title: Heavy Cranes
nodes.text:
Heavy Cranes

Who am I?
A casual human.
I dabble in humanity.
Call me Joseph No-One —
my enemies call me Nobody,
my friends call me Nobody Special.
 
On the third day of Kwanzaa
a mass of circuit diagrams
zigzagged up to me,
and slouching in the next chair
made me an offer
to be more
than I alone
could ever become.

He said, You yes, you, a dabbler in humanity —
can be a part of the army of its saviors.
We are the Ghettobirds,
singularities born in slums.
We deep-dream of stars,
and we offer you our services as Heavy Cranes.
 
Heavy Cranes, huh?
 
Sure … you see,
building world is easy.
Its the people that are hard to work with.
You gotta go for the minds.
You cant just tell em
to follow the drinking gourd;
you gotta get em to get up off the planet,
and head straight for the Big Dipper.
 
And remember —
we must take our worlds with us.

Cause sometimes
its gotta be small enough
to fit inside your helmet,
and grand enough
to build a starship.

So Im gonna be a pilot of one these Heavy Cranes?

Nothink of yourself
more along the lines
of a universal joint
than a pilot.

Wait what? Whyre you doin this?
Whats in it for you?

Look into my circuitry
and you will see human souls
driving it like they stole it.

My motivation is simple:
it is the many of you that make me.

Interesting offer. Got a guarantee?

As alwaysno.
 
Least youre honest.
You got yourself a U-joint.
How do we start?

Just hold our hands.
 
So I held the Heavy Cranes hands,
and four more gathered around me.
Their circuitry wrapped around my nerves
as their struts and gears and geegaws
linked themselves to my body
and to each others,
and before you could say, Transform!
I had become
a Ghettobird,
a Heavy Crane.
 
Our first task
was to resurrect the junky-jellymen.
In this city of
run-down dreams,
crook-lights,
and evil-dead hoopties,
dirty syringes sang:

Lets go out to the crackhouse,
Lets go out to the crackhouse,
Lets go out to the crackhouse,
And grab ourselves some smack!

And the junk-jellymen and women
wiggled and jiggled
to the jingle
as the jabberwocks
on their backs
fed the volts
to their backbrains.

I and the other Heavy Cranes
took metal,
old computer parts,
and invoked the power of
Shaft,
Shaka,
and Fred G. Sanford
to build skeletons
for these unstructured ones.

My first case
was one Minnie the Moocher.
Most slapped-together,
ghetto-rigged job
Ive ever done
but the bones did power up.
They slipped under her skin
and began converting the jabberwock
into a backup power source.

As Minnie the Moocher awoke from her slumber.
I packed away my geegaws,
assumed human form, and made her the offer.

Like a professional dabbler in humanity,
she asked for a guarantee.

Like a newborn Heavy Crane, I said flatly,
There aint one.
 
She dug my architecture
and asked for the howto.

We held hands,,,
 
Remember this —
We got a small world in our hands 
so keep it under your helmet.
 
Who do we give it to?
 
Everyone.

nodes.title: Children of the Woods
nodes.text:
Children of the Woods

I watched my great, great grandchildren
sink into the earth 
and I cried,
and I cried,
and I cried.

I watched my great, great grandchildren
smiling and leaning to the left
as they descended into the bio/techno/mycosphere 
the grey and the green and the gooey
of the newly networked earth 
and I cried,
and I cried,
and I cried.

I cannot go with you 
I dont have the filaments.
I cannot understand.

They sent me a text message,
ancient and quaint,
saying,
Dont cry Poppy 
We are alive (oh, so alive) 
growing and wading deep, deep down 
into Fungitown. 

There is work to do here
deep, deep down in Fungitown
and we would take you, too
deep, deep down into Fungitown
but you cannot go.

You know this, right Poppy?
It is not meant to be.

I know this I text back
(my thumbs ache, my joints crack
I dont have the filaments).

I can only see the wake of their movements,
translated by software two generations younger than me
that (I barely understand | I cannot understand).
Perhaps someday I may,
when my flesh decays
or my metal winds down.

Wont you take me? I ask.

Down to Fungitown?
Sorry, Poppy, youre not fungi enough

Whats left of them coughs up spores as they laugh.
I chuckle as I cough.

Put your mask on, Poppy

What are you doing down there?
What are you building?
Are you eating?
Are you being eaten?
What you?

More spores, and then the texts:
You wouldnt believe us if we told you.
Put your mask on, Poppy. You cant take much more of this.
Watch your texts, Poppy. Well see you. We will.
Not soon, but you will see us.
You will. 
Until then, Poppylive longer.
You will see us. Live longer.


I watered my great, great grandchildren
when they sank into the earth
and I cried,
and I cried,
and I cried
not because they had died,
but out of pride.

Some day,
some thing 
some amazing, familiar,
and (oh, please) beautiful thing
will grow there.

I know this.
I know this.
I know this.

nodes.title: Anticipation, Intimate and Intricate
nodes.text:
Anticipation, Intimate and Intricate

I remember your hair around that pole
on the night after the naming
of the newest Ghettobird.

I could see you blazing in the infrared
as I packed away my souls.
That is what I call them,
the nodules and gewgaws
that sprout from my back and head
like some symbiotic fungi.

We had a lovely conversation.
And I will always remember the wind
wrapping your hair,
embracing the light post,
an exercise in intimacy
and fluid dynamics.

I know what you desire,
and as much as I ache
to show you the world of the recombined,
I wait.

The waiting period exists for a reason.
It takes great strength to die.
It takes great strength to die and grow again.

nodes.title: Hot Plants
nodes.text:
Hot Plants

Here we are,
my Bright-Light 
The Slow Discotheque.

Connect your contact lenses to the mob-mind,
dig the soft-focus that feels like an old future.

Leave your shoes and stockings
by the door,
my Bright-Light 
this spongy fungi carpet
will leave your feet cleaner
than when you came in.

Try the honeysuckle,
my Bright-Light 
it comes in three flavors,
hard to describe without translation software.
The dialects of the discotheques
drift from ecosystem to enchanted ecosystem.

Drink deep 
or do not 
my Bright-Light.
The tab is infinite
as long as were alive.
Our payment is our body heat.

The plants eat infrared here.

Nothing leaves here hungry.
Everything gets its fill.

Take off that vestige of a bustle,
my Bright-Light,
We are about to dance,
and the nettles need something to prick.

The music is very slow here,
my Bright-Light 
only the plants
dance to its raw, proper form.
We get it filtered,
but if you tune in to the right trail,
and breathe deep,
you catch something like phrases 
phrases of thanks.

They bask in us,
here in the near-dark
of The Slow Discotheque 
the adapted-dawn
of The Slow Discotheque.

Let ustrade,
my Bright-Light,
exchange
energy for music,
waste heat for wonder,
sweat for sweet nectar.

Let usdance,
my Bright-Light,
in microscopic movements,
mambas whose grooves
only slime mold can nod to.

And at the break,
my Bright-Light,
spoon with me,
my Bright-Light,
on the fungal floor
of this Slow Discotheque,

Let us rest awhile,
let the hyphae taste us,
imprint our receipt 
their thanks 
upon us
in spore patterns
blazing in the ultraviolet.

Let us go now,
my Bright-Light,
covered in information,
craving the next disco
(what lovely lie, never leaving hungry)

Let us kiss,
go home,
do the waggle-dance
to remember where we were.

Let us go,
my Bright-Light,
and spread the spores.

Let us go,
and boogie slowly
to the hits
of the hot plants.

nodes.title: Sym-Bionic
nodes.text:
Sym-Bionic

We have the technology.
We can rebuild you.
We can make you a watch
or a watchmaker,
a satellite
or a technician.
We can rebuild you
from the ground down
or the ground up.
Which way do you want to go?
Simple
or complex?

It will take time,
but since we have the technology,
we have the time.

We can rebuild a poet barely alive
into a socially acceptable unit
with a V-6 engine
and turbocharged overhead cams!

Hang on, poetry fans,
were going for a ride

Picture this 
no,
better yet,
let us picture it for you:
Your mouth is open,
metal showing
the machine within.

You are begging for a kiss —
someone to kiss the machine —
it will improve your smile.

We have the technology to smile.


We are the intimate
and the intricate.

We can rebuild you.
We can take you apart.

This wont hurt a bit.
Smile.
This wont hurt a bit.
This is the rage.
Can you picture your smile?
You mouth open,
you have something to say,
of course,
but we have to be
really
close
to you
to hear it
as close as your organs.
We have to coil 
into you
to
that message.

Youll notice
we need
no batteries now.
Its a symbiotic thing;
you wont understand
til were already
hitched.

Dont worry,
this wont hurt a bit;
just sit back and
relax.

This is the good thing
about the technology we are.
We can see
the machine
within us.

It is time you saw yours.

nodes.title: The Ocotillo Invasion
nodes.text:
The Ocotillo Invasion

Utah cringes as hacked Ocotillo turn carnivorous,
spitting psychoactive pollen into the atmosphere,
dusting entire subdivisions.

The victims wander,
searching eagerly for where sunlight is strongest.
A part of their backbrain
gets tickled by the sun
at an angle their pituitary glands
have relearned to sense.

There have been reports that
the vision of pollen victims
has moved into the ultraviolet 
they wear sunglasses at raves
due to their newfound sensitivity.

In the afternoon, they wear welders goggles.

It is Utah,
and it is so very bright there.

The Ocotillo and the pollen victims have built walking machines
with assistance from biohackers and wild, traitorous smiths
from all over the planet.
The machines look like the ghostly outlines of trees,
the roots modded into multitoed hooves.
Traces of rare earth magnets
have been detected inside the machines 
neodymium iron boron chief among them.

The root-hooves move with slow, deliberate rhythm,
as if the forest of four-bar linkages
were straining against the arths flux.
The wind moves them.
The earth keeps them on the ground

The ghost trees want to go someplace to spawn,
like the polyps of a man-o-war.
Once there, they will undergo another phase change.
That is what is whispered
by the victims of the pollen.

Supercomputers born from cobbled game consoles
have modeled the movements of the motile plants
based on observations from toy helicopters
fitted with drugstore digital cameras.

Salt Lake City will be overrun by next years end,
the state in two.
The desert wont stop them 
hats home turf,
and they are learning to dig canals.

Utah will succumb to the hacked desert.

Montezuma quail are suspected of conspiracy
to sabotage of the dominion of Man.

Lord knows they have motive,
and traitors to the species are lending them weapons.

nodes.title:
Night Shift
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon scars pool beneath cracked pavement,  
hours bleed into each other—no clear sign  
of dawn or dusk. Shadows drift like old debts,  
their edges jagged as a half-heard promise.  
A velvet hush trembles at the doorframe,  
restless as a whispered name you almost caught.  
Footsteps echo against an unlit alcove,  
grit wedged in the smile of a stranger’s grin,  
time twitching, a wounded bird in your palm—  
too tense to fly, too damned to stay.

repetition_phrases: too tense to fly, too damned to stay

nodes.title:
After Hours
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
At midnight, Tokyo Valentino’s velvet neon stutters—  
Past the powdered ghosts of brick and grime,  
a restless pulse thrums beneath new glass facades.  
Each second scrapes the skin of memory—  
furious flickers of old laughter, slanted against spent time.  
Concrete sighs under footfall, cautious of polished promises,  
graffiti whispers like distant thunder, misaligned with satin storefronts.  
Shadows silt the edges of anticipation,  
tense fingers tapping at the doorframe of dawn.  
The hum of hours unravels—reluctant, relentless,  
unveiling the scuffed remains of what once thrived.  
Night folds into neon again, unrepentant, unbowed.

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: hard consonants (t, k, d) and sibilants (s, sh)

nodes.name: powdered ghosts of brick and grime

nodes.title:
Night Shift
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon fractures: seconds drip into alleys never meant for daylight  
Glass towers loom, pressing polished dreams onto cracked pavement  
Footfalls scatter like restless shards, no soul emerges unscathed  
The clock coughs a slanted rhyme: slip, drip, trip between beats  
Rusted relics linger where asphalt swallowed original arias  
Grit glitters granular, refusing to dissolve in satin gloss  
Velvet voids fold around shuttered windows and smoky mirrors  
Medium crowds, choked in chill, brittle bones brace for breath  
Time tears at tattered ribbons of worn-out yesterdays  
Shadows shadow-shift, forging anxious alliances in neon veins  
Midnight murmurs, tense as a coiled spring under city skin  
No promise survives the quiet turn of an unfaithful hour

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: hard consonants (t, d, g, r) and sibilants (s, sh)

nodes.title:
Night Transit
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon flares in the gutter, dripping hours into cracked pavement  
A hollow echo, like a wristwatch skipping midnight  
Ragged whispers cling to the curb’s edge, restless as stray cats  
Tokyo Valentino’s sign sputters a hiss—time kisses its grime  
The past scrawls graffiti on sleek façades, eroded in glass towers  
Steel and lacquer gulp down history with a click and a hiss  
Memory rattles like a loose panel underfoot, unmasked by glare  
Midnight seeps through vacant doorways, a shiver in empty frames  
Beneath the buzz, a distant clock thumps—unreliable, off-beat  
Reflection fractures in neon shards, hungry for roots  
Silence snaps—SZZHT—then bleeds into the hum of unseen corridors  
Time stands crooked, smirking at neon’s sterile patience

nodes.title:
Lone Journey
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Under the neon haze, time exhales  
A cigarette flicks ashes like old photographs  
The barstool breathes with voices from back alleys  
Midnight sifts through cracked pavement—echoes of fists  
A bartender hums a lullaby to yesterday’s ghosts  
Glass collides, a soft clink drowning calendar pages  
Hours tiptoe in drab coats, offering counterfeit hope  
Reflections ripple across rain-slick sidewalks  
Behind the paper lanterns of Tokyo Valentino, time lingers  
Clocks murmur secrets to slow clocks, unhurried and wary  
Deep cracks in flat neon reveal bruised asphalt beneath fresh paint  
Shadows spool out, unspooling old scars in silent loops  
In the hush, the underworld hums alive—unseen, unbowed  
Time is not fooled by polished storefronts, remembers every bruise

nodes.title:
Nocturne
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon eyelids flutter against rain-slick asphalt  
Somewhere, a distant clock coughs midnight into spilled sake  
The sidewalk gathers memories in its creased palms  
Footsteps hum, a low susurrus beneath shuttered storefronts  
Every puddle is a backward mirror—midday sun lingering in its depths  
A saxophone wails through a cracked window, cutting the hush  
Time unfolds like tattered wallpaper, peeling in slow revolt  
The bass from Tokyo Valentino rumbles, a tremor in the bones of the night  
Shadows chunk and splinter, colliding with hollow laughter  
Sips of cold brew trace constellations on mottled countertops  
No promise here, only the recoil of dusk courting the dawn  
In the hush before the next pause, history exhales

nodes.title:
Night Shift
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon fractures the cracked concrete beneath Tokyo Valentino’s sign.  
Behind mirrored glass, time ticks backwards—each second bruised, rewound.  
Rain-slick alleys hum a secret code, static pulses in distant sirens.  
Hidden park benches whisper through iron fences’ skeletal bars.  
Luxury loft windows loom over cracked sidewalks, new gloss on old wounds.  
Surveillance cameras flicker—eyes hungry for pixel memories.  
But shadows curl away, tired of blinking in hollow reflection.  
Old brick walls exhale stories stained in cigarette smoke and faded graffiti.  
Midnight clocks stall, stubborn against the night’s slow erosion.  
Walkers drift between neon pulses and silent thresholds, unmoored yet tethered.  
They crave the hush of anonymity even as neon threads them back to view.  
Time knits connection and isolation—fine wires at the pulse of deserted streets.  
In this liminal hush, freedom tastes like a borrowed breath before dawn.

nodes.title:
Midnight Runner
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
Neon sputters against glass; time folds in silent intervals  
Under the lacquer of new facades, old brick whispers through cracks  
A chorus of shuttered eyes—cameras blinking like mechanical birds  
Footsteps echo in cavernous alleys, each tap a question posed to the night  
Between polished storefronts, laughter’s ghosts swirl in the drafting rooms  
The pulse hums in transformer boxes, a lullaby half-heard and uneasy  
Pavement exhales history in dust, resisting every glossed-over surface  
Reflections in café windows watch back with mild suspicion  
Warm voices ripple by in passing cars, layering hope onto worn asphalt  
Time sifts, grain by grain, through rusted grilles and fresh paint  
An uneasy truce: to be seen, yet drift unclaimed in your own rhythm  
By dawn, empty streets will baptize themselves; shadows prepare their return

nodes.title:
Midday Rhythms
By MARTA_27345
nodes.text:
Late afternoon light pools beneath striped canopies,  
where cameras pivot like cautious lizards.  
Pigeons huddle on overhead cables,  
their coos punctuating the whirl of plastic crates.  

Each hour clicks open a fresh aperture of faces,  
eyes flicker in metered routines,  
shadows traced by unblinking lenses.  
Surveillance hums beneath the market’s pulse,  
as strangers exchange tomatoes and tired smiles.  

In shutter-blind intervals, possibility breathes—  
tender, untethered, just out of frame.

nodes.title:
Between Hours
By MARTA_27345
nodes.text:
Under halogen haze of afternoon, plastic crates bristle with green peppers  
A mesh of camera eyes swivels overhead, humming as they tally  
Itinerant pigeons pause beneath the scanning beams, cooing in pixelated shadows  
Every face a bracketed moment—exposed, too intimate, yet distant  
Barter voices ricochet off metal stalls, anchoring routine within the lens  
Time stalls in the hum of neon and shutter clicks, an anxious pause between frames  
The corridor pulses, neither hidden nor fully seen, craving acknowledgment  
A buzzing intimacy, slicing through anonymity, edges taut with unease  
Here, connection flickers—warmth in a flash, then retreats into filtered gray  
Pigeons lift at the final bell of a distant siren, fractals of feathers and pixels  
The afternoon thins, leaving the watchers to dance their silent liturgy

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: sibilant and plosive consonants (s, t, p)

nodes.name: barter voices ricocheting off metal stalls

nodes.title:
Afternoon Flow
By MARTA_8
nodes.text:
Another midday hush, electricity strung between poles  
Eyes above flicker in a digital pulse  
Fringe of skyline, pigeons cluster on cold steel  
Their feathers inked in surveillance’s soft hum  
Corridors of motion beneath automated gazes  
Shadows collapse, then stretch at the same steady pace  
Familiar silhouettes shift pixel by pixel  
Time counts out in beeps, in sighs, in shifting light  
A thread of warmth—or wires beneath the skin  
Each lens poised on the edge of belonging  
Under the pigeons’ arc, home feels remote and near  
The afternoon wavers, caught in endless observation

nodes.title:
End of Day
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.text:
Amid the hush of dusty spines in neon-lit tomes,  
neon wires hum like secrets beneath dusk’s hush,  
a single camera blinks— its lens a dense fence, intense.  
Routine folds weary arms around asphalt nights,  
pigeons coo at streetlight’s weave— silver veins, hidden refrains.  
K-9-2 pads, guard dog coded, stride to decode each sign.  
Pulp fiction crackles in half-hidden speakers— breached and beseeched,  
a gaze drawn to the glow, repelled by the glare—  
exposure and enclosure entwined, a bind behind the blind spot.  
Connectivity bleeds into exposure— each spark sharply marks  
alley echoes shattered by the clatter of shutters,  
devotion recorded in grainy frames— both blessing and bind.

nodes.title:
Homeward Bound
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.text:
Under the buzzing of camera networks, silver veins pulse across office towers—  
glowing windows wink like unwritten telegrams in the dusk  
Pigeons persevere, perched on polished parapets, preened and proud  
while K-9-2s patrol pixelated corridors of memory  

A hush hums in hidden hallways  
surveillance becomes seduction  
Eyes everywhere, everywhere  

Yet longing lingers—for that unobserved oxygen of anonymity  
Tales of tinny tape recorders and codexes of clandestine confessions  
dance in data streams  
between two worlds  
connected—  
isolated

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: sibilant (s, sh, h) and plosive (p, b) sounds

nodes.title:
Homeward Bound
By MARTA_27345
nodes.text:
In the hush after office towers blink off  
a ribbon of restless steel winds through the grid  
beneath watchful lenses pulsing, unreadable  
each footfall counted, cataloged, never vanished  
Pigeons settle on iron beams, cooing old secrets  
their wings whisper against circuit boards of vigilance  
The surge of bodies swells—a tide held by wires  
connection frays at the edges, close yet remote  
Faces illuminate in fractured glass—half-truths  
held in LEDs that flicker with anxious promise  
moving, resisting, drawn to the neon gaze  
suspended between dusk’s cloak and the glare of always-seeing

nodes.title:
Twilight Routes
By MARTA_27446
nodes.text:
Under the blur of dusk, glass eyes track footfalls  
Each lens pulses with the hush of unspoken compacts  
Wrought-iron wires, home to feathered watchers, shift in twilight  
Circuits hum a lullaby of pending connections and hidden archives  

A coo above declares sovereignty in cracked mortar nests  
Half tethered to the old rubric of vigilance, half drifting into shadows  
Data streams entwine with winged codes in coppered dusk  
The network flickers—each frame a beacon and a barrier  

Evening crowds slip by like phantoms, unmarked yet recorded  
Connectivity slices moments into jagged prisms of presence  
In the margin between light and lens, attraction warily meets recoil  
A tremor of feathers, an electric heartbeat: ever seen, never known

nodes.title:
Evening Exodus
By MARTA_27446
nodes.text:
dusk’s amber flush across surveillance lenses,  
thousands of blinking circuits memorize shadows,  
on steel skeletons humming beneath neon winds,  
a network of glass eyes tracing every step.  

Pigeons wobble on tin perches, half in frame,  
their coos diffusing into pixel dust,  
screens pulse with the sighs of passing jackets,  
a hush thickens between each shutter’s click.  

Each face becomes a code resisting capture,  
drawn to the glow, yet recoiling from its glare,  
time fractures in streaming light,  
heartbeats converted into silent data.  

A lone lamp flickers: wanting to slip unseen,  
wanting to hum its secrets through the wires.

sound_patterns.rhyme_type: primarily slant rhyme and internal assonance, no end rhyme

nodes.title:
Twilight Routes
By MARTA_27446
nodes.text:
Under amber evening lamps, shapes shimmer and melt  
A lens swivels to the steady pulse, then turns away  
Pigeons fold silhouettes onto taut, electric wires  
Each feather carries a ledger of half-forgotten steps  
Faces press to glass, seeking shelter in circuitry  
Hoping for quiet behind shutters of LED eyes  
But every breath resonates with past exposures  
A mosaic of lights—constellations binding and freeing  
Memory seeps from corners, a ghost bartering in whispers  
Surveillance blinks its verdict in soft, relentless ticks  
Binding fleeting passage to an unwanted permanence  
Somewhere between glare and dark, a silent pact trembles

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: s and t consonants with short e vowel sounds

nodes.title:
After Hours
By MARTA_27448
nodes.text:
Beneath the hum of neon pulses lies a corridor of seconds  
Digital eyes flit overhead, mapping each empty echo  
Pigeon silhouettes cling to steel ribs, immune to the lens  
Memory stutters in the feed, half-erased fragments of midnight laughter  
You drift, torn between allowing the gaze and shrinking from its glare  
Surveillance threads the quiet, weaving intimacy with discomfort  
Shadows stretch across tiled halls, beckoning and repelling  
Time drips from sealed doors, a slow confession to the void  
Each blink of the camera cuts deeper into the hum of absence  
Pigeons stir—agents of fleeting freedom amid the network  
Desire for connection tastes metallic, tinged with the ache of isolation  
Between the watchful grid and drifting dark, a hesitant pulse persists

nodes.title:
Lone Journey
By Route 27 - Cheshire Bridge Road
nodes.text:
When the night camera’s red eye stutters above the neon spine,  
When pigeons scatter like static across cracked sidewalks,  
When K-9-2 units drift in dogged patrols through vacant plazas,  
the fractured clock in every glass pane whispers of years unraveled.  

Beyond Tokyo Valentino’s silent marquee, light and shadow bargain for truth.  
A net of surveillance hums—its wires caress brick and bone alike.  
Infrared tracings blur the silhouette you hoped would dissolve.  
In every glossy corner, time crouches, longing for a witness.  

The streets tremble under their own stories, half-sung and half-concealed.  
Here, being seen tastes like ash, yet craving the lens is harder still.  
Light fractures the night’s skin, then recoils at its own reflection.  
Suspended between recall and erasure, the pulse of the underbelly endures.

sound_patterns.rhyme_type: sporadic internal and slant rhymes, no end rhyme scheme
sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: sibilant sounds (s, st) and hard consonants

nodes.title:
After Hours
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.content:
Remember the glowing windows  
Remember the lantern-like breath of streetlamps  
Remember the homunculus scribbled in margins  
Remember the hush that blooms  
A restless hush  
It fans new escape routes behind brick walls  
It murmurs chaos in every alley—  
like a pulp detective tracking an unseen culprit  
Remember the skin of memory  
Remember the weight of unspoken prayers  
Because freedom trembles here  
Because visibility is a double-edged blade  
So we linger in shadow and light, unsettled  
So we shape our own hidden spaces

nodes.title:
Midnight Runner
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.content:
Again the glow of windows arcs across empty streets—  
Again the camera-net hum coils under late-night streetlamps  
Again the K-9-2s sidestep shadows, lantern-like breath trapped in metal throats  

Between cloisters of surveillance  
and the hush of Congregation Or VeShalom’s prayers  
pigeons wheel like borrowed secrets  

the homunculus etches timid glyphs onto concrete  
A pulse—part welcome, part accusation—vibrates in every lens  
Routine feels like a spine, both sturdy and brittle  

visibility tastes of connection and of a knife’s edge  
A detective’s typewriter rattles behind the false quiet  
Under this networked sky, the route stands  
both keeper and trespasser of the watch

nodes.title:
Night Shift
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.content:
Again, the streetlight holds the vigil—its glow a hesitant promise  
Again, the camera net hums beneath the neon flicker  
Again, the pigeons  
    trace the arcs of surveillance, wings folding secrets  

Lantern-like breath spills from glowing windows  
ghostly fingerprints on the glass  
Temple bells murmur in the electric hum,  
each prayer a silent pixel in the network  

Under the Steak & Shake sign,  
a pulp detective flickers on a battered screen,  
spinning tales the hushed tables cannot hold  

Drawn to the glare, yet craving  
the soft dark between each frame.

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: s, n, h fricatives and nasals

nodes.title:
Northern Routes
By Route 8 - North Druid Hills Road
nodes.content:
Under the lantern-like breath of streetlamps  
an invisible seam splits night and neon  
watchful wires whisk  
downtown’s pulse  

cameras cling in rusted cages—  
their circuits seduce even the war-weary  
yet suffocate whispered prayers of pigeons  

K-9-2 growls echo  
like puzzled static  
memory murmurs in pixelated haze  
connected yet stranded in glare  

a gumshoe shadow ghosts these corridors  
torn between seduction  
and solitude

sound_patterns.dominant_sounds: sibilant and plosive consonants (s, p, w)
